claims.text: Additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi parts contain residual stress.
Additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi parts contain porosity.
The proposed intervention is HIP at 1000°C and 100 MPa for 2 hours.
HIP under the stated conditions will reduce porosity in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
HIP under the stated conditions will reduce residual stress in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Thermally activated diffusion contributes to the effects of HIP on AlCrFeNiSi.
Plastic deformation under hydrostatic pressure contributes to the effects of HIP on AlCrFeNiSi.
HIP will reduce segregation relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
HIP will limit defect formation relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
HIP will improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi relative to conventional fabrication.
HIP-treated additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi will have improved tensile strength, yield strength, or elongation relative to untreated additively manufactured material.
Optimization of the specified HIP conditions may be necessary to obtain optimal results.

contradictions.description: The stated hypothesis uses conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi as the comparator, whereas the falsification experiment compares HIP-treated material only with untreated additively manufactured material. Thus the experiment does not directly test the stated baseline-relative outcome.
